$comment: Hand-curated pre-season intelligence, compiled from public FPL coverage.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: the app cannot search the web. It can only call the FPL API. Anything
that comes from journalism, press conferences or community consensus has to be brought in
deliberately, and that means somebody writes it down here, dated and sourced, where it can be
argued with. Nothing in this file is scraped, inferred or invented by the model.
It matters most right now and least later. Before a ball is kicked there are no stats for the
new season, so this is real evidence. Once matches are played the API's own data takes over
and 'staleAfter' below stops these adjustments being applied to a season they no longer
MATCHING: entries are matched on web_name plus club short name, both as the FPL API reports
them. A name that matches nothing is reported, never silently ignored - see `fpl intel`.
EVERY adjustment is a tunable number, and setting eliteConsensusWeight to 0 disables the
eliteConsensusWeight: xPts added to a player owned by essentially every elite manager,
scaled by the consensus figure below. It is a nudge, never a gate - a player this file
loves still has to earn his place through the model and the rules engine.
availabilityOverridesEnabled: whether the flags below may reduce a player's availability.
They can only ever make a player LESS available, never more - see the loader.

eliteConsensus.note: Owned by essentially every elite manager and above 70% overall ownership. Record £15.5m price after 239 points last season. Three attractive home fixtures in the opening five.
The biggest constant in elite squads. Opens against Hull City and Ipswich Town, with secure starts and captaincy appeal.

contextNotes: The 2026 World Cup final was played on 19 July 2026. Players who reached the final or the third-place playoff did not report back to club training until 9-12 August, leaving under eleven days of preparation before the 21 August deadline. Expect rotation and cameos rather than full starts for that group.
Nine clubs begin the season with a new head coach or an unresolved managerial situation, so last season's roles are a weaker guide than usual.
Manchester City and Arsenal are modelled as a tier of their own for the opening fixtures.
Defenders dominated the 2025/26 scoring charts, which the DefCon rules continue to reward.
